text:
$SPCX CEO: Short-term compute contracts are renewing at higher prices per watt

"I think we're going to face a shortage of super intelligence compute. And that shortage is going to remain for a long time. So I think the smart move is to do short-term contracts and to and essentially to make -- to place the bet on useful intelligence per watt increasing rapidly, which obviously has done.

"And also, if you look at, say, how are our short-term contracts renewing? Are they renewing at higher dollars per watt or lower? And we see them renewing at higher dollars per watt, not lower dollars per watt."

en_summary: @StockSavvyShay cites Elon saying robot RAM needs will exceed everything else on Earth. $TSLA making 10M Optimus a year at 72GB each needs ~720 petabytes of memory, bullish for $MU and $SKHY, though robots use LPDDR rather than HBM, making it a volume story.
text:

Pretty wild for $MU and $SKHY as AI expands beyond data centers although robots use LPDDR rather than HBM so this could become a much bigger volume story.

name: Jensen Huang
zh_summary: @JensenHuang thanks Berlin for GTC: Europe is building its AI ecosystem; highlights DSX POD Vera Rubin modular factories delivered ready to run, the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, NVIDIA OpenShell for safety, and new physical AI customers in AI-RAN and robotaxis.
en_summary: @JensenHuang thanks Berlin for GTC: Europe is building its AI ecosystem; highlights DSX POD Vera Rubin modular factories delivered ready to run, the NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, NVIDIA OpenShell for safety, and new physical AI customers in AI-RAN and robotaxis.
text:
I was the opening act for a family of ducks.

Thank you, Berlin. What a GTC.

Europe is building its AI ecosystem and economy, from AI factories to agents to robots.

DSX POD: Vera Rubin modular factories built, cabled and tested in the factory, then delivered ready to produce intelligence.

Agents: models, harnesses, sandboxes, knowledge and tools. NVIDIA Agent Toolkit brings the pieces together so companies control what their agents know, access and do.  NVIDIA OpenShell enhances safety.

Physical AI: new customers across AI-RAN, robotaxis and robotics.

Personal AI: after four years building with Microsoft, RTX Spark brings personal agents to the Windows PC.

Thank you to President @EmmanuelMacron, Prime Minister @andyburnham and Chancellor @bundeskanzler for hosting me. Great to celebrate Sferical One with Sweden’s technology leaders. And thank you to President @TokayevKZ for the warm welcome.

And to our partners and NVIDIA teams: thank you for making it happen.

The keynote is here: https://youtu.be/rF1EsryCAwc

name: Fireside Alpha
zh_summary: (Reposted by @carlquintanilla) @firesidealpha says Verizon CEO Dan Schulman operates on the assumption that everything SpaceX says it will do, it will do flawlessly, and takes its terrestrial moves quite seriously.
en_summary: (Reposted by @carlquintanilla) @firesidealpha says Verizon CEO Dan Schulman operates on the assumption that everything SpaceX says it will do, it will do flawlessly, and takes its terrestrial moves quite seriously.
text:
BREAKING: Verizon CEO admits he assumes everything SpaceX says it will do, it will do, and execute flawlessly, and says he takes its terrestrial moves "quite seriously"

Dan Schulman (CEO): “I also operate under the assumption that everything SpaceX says they will do, they will do, and that they will execute flawlessly. That’s my operating assumption on it. I think to assume anything else, makes no sense from my perspective."

"And everything that we’ve seen so far, all of their announcements, everything we’re hearing in the market, and I’ll talk about that in just a second, is so far the path that we’ve basically predicted that they would do."

"We always knew that they needed a terrestrial network to have any chance at providing a competitive service. I don’t really need to re-review the satellite beam physics, but just suffice to say that without a terrestrial network, their addressable market for broadband services is relatively small.”

"It’s in very rural areas, and their service just can’t compete with a terrestrial network. In suburban and urban areas where like 98% of our revenues are, we’re somewhere between 100 to 1,000 times more efficient than they are. And when you think about wireless, it’s even more difficult with them to compete on a satellite basis."

"And so I think that SpaceX realizes this, and they’re exploring a potential path to creating a terrestrial network. It’s not surprising they said it on their call, so I think we should take it quite seriously.

They're going to look at 65,000–80,000 macro sites. They're going to need backhaul, RAN, and a tremendous amount of spectrum. It's going to take a minimum of four to six years to fully build that out. It's going to cost hundreds and hundreds of billions of dollars, I assume somewhere between $300 billion and $500 billion.

Then they need to build retail, customer service, back office systems, et cetera. All of that gets them basically the same network and same capabilities and same cost structure as what we have today.
